task.description:
Implement type coercion rules in the DSL evaluator per DSL-05 and the design in src/design/dsl-05-coercion.md. Modify src/expr/mod.zig evaluateNode() to implement:

1. Coercion logic for arithmetic operators (add_expr, mul_expr, unary_neg):
   - int64 ↔ float64 automatic promotion (int64 → float64 when mixed)
   - Both operands same type → no coercion needed
   - Non-numeric types in arithmetic → structured EvalError

2. Comparison operators (cmp_expr):
   - Same-type comparison → direct comparison
   - int64 vs float64 → explicit error (no silent coercion)
   - Other mixed-type comparisons → explicit error
   - null compared to anything except null → returns null (three-valued logic)
   - null == null → true
   - null != null → false

3. Boolean operators (and_expr, or_expr, not_expr) with three-valued logic:
   - null AND x → if x is false → false, else null
   - null OR x → if x is true → true, else null
   - NOT null → null

4. Dot path resolution with null propagation:
   - Accessing a field on null → null (not an error)

5. No automatic string coercion — string to/from other types only via built-in functions

Validate: zig build exits 0, zig build test passes.
acceptance_criteria: zig build exits 0 with no 'error set' warnings
zig build test passes all existing and new tests
Arithmetic with mixed int64/float64 promotes int64 to float64
Comparison between int64 and float64 returns EvalError (no silent coercion)
null == null returns true; null != null returns false
null == any-non-null returns null; null != any-non-null returns null
Dot-path access on failing intermediate returns null, not error
String coercion never automatic — explicit built-in functions only

result.summary: Implemented type coercion rules in DSL evaluator per DSL-05. evaluateNode() now handles all Node variants: arithmetic (add_expr, mul_expr, unary_neg) with int64-float64 promotion, comparison (cmp_expr) with three-valued null logic, boolean (and_expr, or_expr, not_expr) with Kleene K3 logic, and dot_path with null propagation. No automatic string coercion.
